title: Apply Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to Zero
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a positive integer k, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any subarray of size k from the array and decrease each of its elements by 1.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a positive integer k, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any subarray of size k from the array and decrease each of its elements by 1. Determine whether it is possible to make all elements of the array equal to 0. Return true if it is possible, otherwise return false. Note that a subarray is a contiguous segment of the array.
constraints: An operation chooses k consecutive elements and decreases each by one.
Operations may be repeated but array values may never become negative.
Return whether all elements can become zero.
hints: Scan left to right while tracking the active decrement contributed by earlier windows.
At each index, the remaining value forces exactly that many operations to begin there.
Schedule their expiration k positions later with a difference array; fail if negative or a needed window exceeds the boundary.
No later window can change an earlier index, so the forced greedy choice is necessary and, when all choices fit, sufficient.
editorial: No later window can change an earlier index, so the forced greedy choice is necessary and, when all choices fit, sufficient.

tests.explanation: Applying the forced operations from left to right reduces every entry exactly to zero.
The middle demand cannot be satisfied without making a neighboring value negative.
